verdicts.note: Never held county office and runs on fixing the office from outside (S1, S2). Kept at 1 rather than 2: 20 years of licensed practice and GOP precinct/state-committee roles make him a practitioner-challenger, not a maximal outsider/renewal case.

The spending axis asks whether government under-invests or fails to manage and audit what it spends. Hollingsworth's cited evidence (S1, S2) is about appraisal accuracy and equity: who pays what share of levies the assessor does not set, training appraisers to professional standards, and supporting staff 'without micromanagement'. Nothing in the dossier concerns the office's budget, expenditures, audits or new programs; his own dossier's scoring note says the 'fair share' language is about accuracy, not tax or spending levels. Rosenau also claims 'clear standards that promote fairness and accountability' (his S1), so the score draws a spending contrast the evidence does not show. Omit.

Incumbent since 2021, re-elected 2022, three years chairing the regional assessors and a seat on the state association board, running on his record (S1). Tenure is about five years, not long, but against a challenger who has never held the office -2 is the fair placement and consistent with the package's other incumbent scores.

Direction checked: he says he has worked for 'fair and sustainable property tax relief' and broader exemptions for seniors, people with disabilities, farmers and small businesses (S1), and in 2023 described the senior/disability exemption as protection against tax foreclosure (S3). That is pole_a (reducing the burden); magnitude 1 at medium fits advocacy for relief through exemptions by an official who stresses he does not set tax levels (S2). S1 and S3 exist in his frontmatter and support the claim.
